boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Named public destinations along campus-adjacent and downtown Houghton corridors.

cards.title: College Avenue Park
cards.subtitle: College Avenue corridor, between campus and downtown
cards.notes: Pause at the deck and seating area for a waterway view while walking between campus and downtown.
cards.short_summary: A compact College Avenue stop built around a deck, seats, and the waterway.
cards.evidence_claim: The City describes College Avenue Park as a pocket park with a deck and seating area for viewing the Keweenaw Waterway between Michigan Tech and downtown.
cards.access_notes: Use the College Avenue route between campus and downtown.

cards.title: Carnegie Museum of the Keweenaw
cards.subtitle: Huron Street corridor at Montezuma Avenue
cards.notes: Check the changing exhibits and programs in the former Carnegie library building at 105 Huron Street.
cards.short_summary: A public local-history museum at the Huron–Montezuma corner.
cards.evidence_claim: The City says the Carnegie Museum is at 105 Huron Street, is open to the public, has changing regional exhibits and programs, and charges no visit fee.
cards.access_notes: Confirm standard versus summer hours before going.

cards.title: Dee Stadium
cards.subtitle: East Lakeshore Drive corridor
cards.notes: Look for the hockey-history exhibit or a public-skating slot; bring skates because the venue does not rent them.
cards.short_summary: A historic waterfront rink and community center with a hockey-history exhibit.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies Dee Stadium at 700 East Lakeshore Drive as a historic ballroom and ice rink with weekly free public skating and a hockey-history exhibit.
cards.access_notes: Public-skating times can change for games or tournaments; check the posted ice schedule.

cards.title: Bridgeview Park
cards.subtitle: M-26 / Lakeshore Drive waterfront corridor
cards.notes: Use the seasonal launch as a clear starting point for a paddle route, then return along the waterfront.
cards.short_summary: A waterfront park with a seasonal kayak and stand-up-paddleboard launch.
cards.evidence_claim: The City states that a seasonal kayak/SUP launch operates in Bridgeview Park from May through October.
cards.access_notes: The kayak/SUP launch is seasonal, May–October.

cards.title: Houghton Waterfront Trail
cards.subtitle: Lakeshore Drive waterfront corridor
cards.notes: Walk, run, or bike a segment of the paved waterfront route and use it to link downtown parks.
cards.short_summary: A paved, barrier-free waterfront route connecting Houghton destinations.
cards.evidence_claim: The City describes the Houghton Waterfront Trail as a 4.5-mile paved, barrier-free route for walkers, joggers, and bicyclists.
cards.access_notes: The trail connects the Waterfront Recreation area/RV Park and Nara Nature Park.

cards.title: Raymond C. Kestner Waterfront Park
cards.subtitle: Lakeshore Drive waterfront corridor
cards.notes: Use the picnic area, beach, pavilion, or waterfront connection as a daylight break from the downtown blocks.
cards.short_summary: A five-acre waterfront park with beach, picnic, and pavilion facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: The City’s recreation plan identifies Kestner Park as a five-plus-acre waterfront park with a swimming beach, picnic area, pavilion, restrooms, and band shell.
cards.source_title: City of Houghton Recreation and Natural Resource Conservation Plan
cards.access_notes: Follow the waterfront corridor; facilities are maintained seasonally.

cards.title: Chutes and Ladders Play Area
cards.subtitle: Lakeshore Drive at Kestner Waterfront Park
cards.notes: Visit this named play area as part of a Kestner Park waterfront stop; pair it with the nearby picnic facilities.
cards.short_summary: A children’s play area within Kestner Waterfront Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The City says the Chutes and Ladders play area is part of Kestner Waterfront Park and continues to be maintained and improved.
cards.access_notes: Located within Kestner Waterfront Park on the waterfront route.

cards.title: East Houghton Waterfront Park
cards.subtitle: Lakeshore Drive / waterfront trail corridor
cards.notes: Use the boardwalk connection, pavilion area, or small-watercraft launch to extend a waterfront-trail outing eastward.
cards.short_summary: A waterfront-trail park with pavilion, boardwalk, and small-watercraft access.
cards.evidence_claim: The City says East Houghton Waterfront Park sits on the waterfront trail, has a kayak and small-sailboat launch, and includes the Houghton Skatepark.
cards.access_notes: The City places it just west of the Super 8 motel; pavilion reservations are available May–September.

cards.title: Nara Nature Park
cards.subtitle: US-41 corridor, east of campus
cards.notes: Choose a trail activity—hike, bike, ski, or snowshoe—and use the public chalet for its interpretive display.
cards.short_summary: A 100-acre park linked to Michigan Tech’s trail system.
cards.evidence_claim: The City describes Nara Nature Park as a 100-acre park two miles east of campus, linked to Michigan Tech trails for hiking, biking, skiing, and snowshoeing.
cards.access_notes: The City states that the public chalet is open daily from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m.; trail conditions vary by season.

cards.title: Nara Nature Trail Boardwalk
cards.subtitle: US-41 corridor at Nara Nature Park
cards.notes: Follow the elevated boardwalk along the Pilgrim River for benches, fishing sites, and water-access viewpoints.
cards.short_summary: A 4,500-foot elevated boardwalk tracing both banks of the Pilgrim River.
cards.evidence_claim: The City states that Nara Nature Trail Boardwalk is 4,500 feet long and includes fishing sites, benches, and kayak/canoe-launch access along the Pilgrim River.
cards.access_notes: Use Nara Nature Park access and follow posted trail conditions.
